newsitem.title: BELGIUM: General Affairs Council dominated by IGC.
newsitem.headline: General Affairs Council dominated by IGC.

text.p: The inter-governmental conference will be the main theme of the General Affairs Council which meets in Luxembourg on Monday and Tuesday.

As EU member states seek to wrap up details of a draft new EU treaty, the Council will devote Monday afternoon and Tuesday morning to treaty issues such as CFSP decision-making and financing, institutional issues in the follow-up to the Noordwijk conclave and employment, the environment and internal market and flexibility.
The remainder of the issues will be taken up on Monday morning, many issues having been deferred to save time until the next Council meeting. They include:
* Former Yugoslavia. The Council will discuss the replacement for the current High Representative Carl Bildt and the kind of support he should be given.
* Market access in the EU for least developed countries, the aim being to extend the maximum available preferential treatment to the world's poorest countries from 1998.

* Humane trapping standards. Although the final say will lie with the Environment Council, the General Affairs Council will look at the state of play on talks with Canada and Russia, keeping in mind the fact that talks with the United States are still unresolved.

* The European observatory on racism and xenophobia. The Council must seek agreement on one final issue -- where will the observatory be based. Although all member states have submitted applications, Vienna has emerged as the clear favourite.
* Transatlantic relations. The ministers will be briefed on the May 28 EU-U.S. Summit and negotiations on the mutual recognition agreement with the United States.
* EU-Japan Summit. The Commission and Presidency will report on preparations for the EU-Japan summit scheduled for June 25 in the Hague.

* Hong Kong. The Council is expected to welcome the broad lines of the Commission's communication on future relations with Hong Kong and look into how consistency of diplomatic contacts can be achieved with the Government of the Special Administrative Region within its areas of responsibility after the hand over to China.
* EU overseas territories. The Council will look at the rice import regime for these countries.

* Albania. The ministers will discuss the state of play in Albania and how it can help in the preparation of the electoral process it sees as essential to stabilise the country. It will discuss, for example, the contribution of the OSCE to the monitoring process. Ministers are expected to adopt a document defining the overall EU effort in Albania.
* The Middle East peace process. Ministers will take stock of developments in the region and discuss steps the EU could take to help relaunch the peace process.
* The Great Lakes. The Council will review the situation in former Zaire in light of the presidency led-mission there.
* Iran. The Council will discuss the state of play as regards the return of EU ambassadors to Iran.
* Switzerland. The ministers will review bilateral negotiations, aware that the latest proposal on the crucial transport dossier from Berne has been deemed unacceptable.
